name: Cerebrolysin

card.summary: A porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved for stroke and dementia in many countries, discussed by forum users as an "iqmaxxing" nootropic.
card.note: Injectable prescription product; nootropic use in healthy people is not studied.

quick.overview:
Cerebrolysin is an injectable mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and amino acids prepared from porcine brain protein. It is marketed by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and used in many countries as an adjunct for stroke, brain injury and dementia.

On looksmax.org it appears in threads about "iqmaxxing" and "brainmaxxing", where members ask whether it helps studying or exams. It is not an appearance compound, and no studies have tested it in healthy people for cognition.
quick.mechanism: Preclinical studies report that it mimics neurotrophic factor activity and promotes neurogenesis in rodent stroke and Alzheimer models, including through the Sonic hedgehog pathway.
quick.risks: Human trials are in patients with neurological disease. Being an animal-derived injectable, it is a prescription product where approved; members mention obtaining it from unofficial sources.

lead: Cerebrolysin is a mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and free amino acids produced by enzymatic breakdown of porcine brain proteins, described as mimicking neurotrophic factors [1][4]. It is manufactured by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and given by injection or infusion [1].

It is approved in many countries for neurological conditions such as stroke, traumatic brain injury and dementia [1]. Human trials have been conducted in post-stroke recovery, including the CARS randomized trial and a meta-analysis of nine randomized trials [3][6].
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a cognitive enhancer. No trial has examined it for appearance outcomes; one small registered study listed hair repigmentation during therapy [11].

paras: Laboratory studies in rats reported that Cerebrolysin increased neurogenesis after experimental stroke and improved functional outcome [2], and that the Sonic hedgehog pathway mediated this effect [5]. A review describes it as a neuropeptide preparation that mimics endogenous neurotrophic factors and, in dementia models, reduces beta-amyloid deposition and tau phosphorylation [4].

The CARS trial randomized stroke patients to Cerebrolysin or saline for 21 days and assessed upper-limb motor function at day 90 [3]. A meta-analysis of nine randomized trials examined its safety and efficacy in early post-stroke recovery [6], and an Asian double-blind trial studied acute ischemic stroke [7]. Registered trials listed include stroke, traumatic brain injury, Down syndrome and preterm infants [8][9][10]. A 5-person registered study examined hair repigmentation during Cerebrolysin therapy [11]. No studies found in healthy people for cognitive enhancement or for appearance outcomes.

Looksmax.org threads include a member considering it before an entrance exam, a thread titled as a deep dive into "iqmaxxing", and others asking about "brainmaxx" use [12][13][14][15]. Members debate whether nootropics in general are "cope".

timeline.event: Grokipedia credits Gerhart Harrer at Innsbruck with pioneering enzymatic hydrolysis of brain tissue [1]

lore.intro: Cerebrolysin appears in looksmax.org nootropic threads, typically asked about for studying and exams [12][13].

claims.claim: Cerebrolysin boosts intelligence and study performance ("iqmaxxing").
claims.believers: Members consider it for exams and language learning and ask about timing and sourcing [12][13][14].
claims.experts: Published human trials are in neurological patients; no published studies have tested it for cognitive enhancement in healthy people.

claims.claim: It supports brain recovery and neurogenesis.
claims.experts: Rodent studies report increased neurogenesis [2][5]; stroke trials and a meta-analysis have evaluated its use in patients [3][6].
